name: sram_cim_macro
display_name: Digital SRAM-CIM macro (16 nm, 128 kB, jiang2023a; macro-level constants only)

validity.array_size_assumed: 128 kB of 6T in 128 blocks of 1 kB (64 rows of 128 b); 16 SR groups of 8 blocks each compute one 128-input dot product per cycle, so the macro is one logical core of 128 inputs x 1024 weight vectors of 8-bit weights; 4-bit inputs, 32-bit partial sums, exact digital accumulation (jiang2023a p.2-3)
validity.notes: MACRO-LEVEL constants only, measured at 20 MHz and 0.58 V (jiang2023a p.4), and the cycle time of one evaluation of the macro's logical core (t_cycle, from the outputs per clock cycle and the measured clocks, p.2-4). Chip-level rows (periphery, NoC, host, static power) are absent and refuse by name; the backing store is declared by a backing-store override block (CL5, CL7), so an SRAM point is never read without it.

e_mac.derivation: 12.6 TOPS/W non-weight-stationary at 8b W x 4b A, 20 MHz: 2 / 12.6e12 J = 158.7 fJ per MAC (1 MAC = 2 OPs); weight-stationary with 20x reuse 23.8 TOPS/W = 84.0 fJ (the band's low end). The non-WS anchor is the one a CIM activation reads.

t_cycle.derivation: One step of the value window is one evaluation of the macro's logical core (128 inputs x 1024 weight vectors, the sram_cim_macro bundle: 16 SR groups of 64 addresses). Outputs per cycle: 'In total 16 32b outputs (SUM[31:0]) are computed each clock cycle for the macro.' (p.2), at the 4-bit input of 'The input activation (IA) driver delivers 128 (4b) IA to all 16 SR groups' (p.2), so the 1024 outputs take 1024 / 16 = 64 cycles. An 8-bit input takes two 4-bit cycles: Fig. 8c (p.4) lists the macro at 'Precision(I/W/O) 8/8/32' with footnote 1 'An 8bW*8bA MAC is defined as two ops', and its 'TP(TOPs) 0.182' closes on 16 x 128 4-bit products per cycle = 1024 8-bit MACs per cycle x 2 ops x 91 MHz = 0.186 TOPS (within 3 %), so 128 cycles per evaluation. Clocks: 'The design is functional down to 20MHz at 0.58V VDDH and 91MHz at 1V VDDH.' (p.3-4) and 'clock period time 0.05us (20MHz)' (p.4). Low: 64 cycles / 91 MHz = 703.3 ns (4-bit inputs at the fastest measured clock); nominal and high: 128 cycles x 50 ns = 6400 ns (8-bit MACs at 20 MHz, the operating point of the profile's energy rows: '12.6TOPs/W at 20MHz' and '23.8TOPs/W (8b) at 20MHz', p.4).
t_cycle.note: DECLARED from the macro's own paper, the arithmetic shown. Every address of the core is counted: a core that uses n of its 1024 neurons reads ceil(n / 16) addresses, so the constant is an upper bound per step for a partly used core. The pipeline fill of the adder trees and ACC blocks and the activation-buffer load are not stated and not counted. A program at 4-bit inputs (activation_bits 4) runs at the band's low half; one wider than 8 bits lies outside the band.

e_write_per_cell.derivation: An 8-bit weight cell is one byte; the array write per byte is bracketed between 1x the measured local-block read byte energy (76 fJ at 20 MHz) and 2x the 91 MHz value (342 fJ), a write being full swing where the read is half swing. Nominal at the log-space centre.
e_write_per_cell.note: houshmand2023benchmarking Table II and Fig. 7 p.6 carry an analytical weight-write term that was not read in this round; it is the cross-check this bracket waits on.

t_write_per_unit.derivation: One write of one 8-bit weight cell (write granularity cell). A 1 kB block is 'arranged into 64 rows containing 128 bits each' (p.2), and a row is read or written in one clock cycle: 'the LBL are left floating until the next read/write cycle' (p.3). One 128-bit row holds 16 weights, so a row written per cycle is 1/16 cycle per cell: 50 ns / 16 = 3.125 ns at 20 MHz ('clock period time 0.05us (20MHz)', p.4; the operating point of the profile's energy rows) and (1/91 MHz) / 16 = 0.687 ns at 91 MHz ('The design is functional down to 20MHz at 0.58V VDDH and 91MHz at 1V VDDH.', p.3-4). The paper states no width of its global data driver, the macro's write port ('a global data driver and activation buffer are provided', p.2): the high end, one byte per 20 MHz cycle, is 50 ns per cell.
t_write_per_unit.note: DERIVED from the macro's own paper, the arithmetic shown; the write port width is the stated assumption the band spans (a 128-bit row per cycle at the nominal and low ends, one byte per cycle at the high end). E-6 (N2 follow-up F5).

write_verify_iterations.derivation: A digital SRAM write is one full-swing write with no verify loop.

endurance_cycles.note: 'about 1e16 cycles over the expected lifetime of embedded SRAM' (scout_chip.md sec. 4.3, SOURCED).

pulses_per_write.derivation: [U-C C-1] An SRAM bit cell is written by one write operation, the unit in which ielmini2018inmemory p.7 counts its 1e16 cycles: one pulse per write.

external_components.name: backing store
external_components.note: the macro holds 128 kB of weights and no store for the rest of a program: the backing store sets the tile write cost (constants.md sec. 5: an 8 KiB tile write costs 0.62-7.7 nJ in the array and 1.33 uJ over DDR3/4 I/O), so an SRAM-CIM point is defined only with its store's transfer energy and time declared, by a named backing_store block
